title: Yet another "segmentation fault" issue with AMD GPU
body: On Linux with an RX 7900 XTX and Ollama 0.3.10, loading larger models fails with `Error: llama runner process has terminated: signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)`, even though Ollama reports enough VRAM. For example, `command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` is about 19 GB and my GPU has 24 GB; `gemma2:27b-instruct-q4_K_M` also fails, while models around 13 GB or smaller load. The logs report about 23.5 GiB available. I think models this size used to work on an older Ollama version, but I do not know which version last worked.

symptoms_visible: Loading `command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` or `gemma2:27b-instruct-q4_K_M` ends with `llama runner process has terminated: signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)`.
Models around 13 GB or smaller load, while Ollama reports more than 22 GiB of available VRAM on my 24 GB RX 7900 XTX.
N0.label: N0 large AMD models segfault

symptoms_visible: A plain `ollama run command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` starts loading all 41 layers through ROCm and then the runner exits with a segmentation fault.
N1.label: N1 configuration and loading log collected

symptoms_visible: The same model still ends in a segmentation fault after setting `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD` as high as 10 GB.
N1_x.label: N1_x GPU-overhead workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: After downgrading to Ollama 0.3.6, `command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` loads successfully and `ollama ps` reports a 21 GB model running 100% on the GPU.
N2.label: N2 temporary downgrade works

symptoms_visible: After removing the Arch package and installing Ollama's official build with bundled ROCm, the same large model still ends in a segmentation fault.
N2_x.label: N2_x official bundled ROCm aftermath

symptoms_visible: The affected large-model workload runs on Ollama 0.3.6 but segfaults on Ollama 0.3.7.
N3.label: N3 regression boundary confirmed

symptoms_visible: On Arch Linux with kernel 6.11.3, the plain command still segfaults during model loading on Ollama 0.3.12, with either ROCm 6.0.2 or the official bundled ROCm.
N4.label: N4 reproducible environment matrix collected

symptoms_visible: The same large model loads and runs correctly with Ollama 0.3.14-rc0.
N5.label: N5 fix verified on release candidate

symptoms_visible: Large models that previously crashed now load and run on the RX 7900 XTX with Ollama 0.3.14 or newer.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Are you setting a custom context size or any other model parameters?
Does a plain `ollama run` command reproduce this?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm not specifying a custom context size or any other parameters. A plain `ollama run command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` reproduces it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only crashes with a very large custom context and does not crash with the model defaults.

question_patterns: Can you share the complete server log around the crash?
What loading command and memory calculation appear immediately before the runner exits?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The log says 22.7 GiB is available and 21.7 GiB is required, requests and offloads all 41 layers to ROCm, and starts the runner with `--no-mmap`. It then waits for the runner and reports that the process terminated with a segmentation fault.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The log reports that the model needs more VRAM than is available and only partially offloads it before an explicit out-of-memory error.
The reported available and required memory differ slightly, but the log still selects all 41 GPU layers and then segfaults.

edges.comment: The reporter supplied the full loading log and confirmed that no custom context or model parameters were involved. The Arch ROCm package list and 32 GB RAM were added alongside this diagnostic evidence.

solution.intent: Treat the crash as inaccurate VRAM prediction and reserve progressively more GPU memory with `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD` or reduce `num_gpu` so fewer layers are loaded.
solution.concrete_example: Set `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD=1073741824`, restart the server, and increase the value if needed so Ollama offloads fewer layers instead of filling VRAM.

edges.comment: Actual workaround attempt from c5-c12. The reporter tested values from 1 GB through 10 GB on 0.3.10 and the model continued to segfault, falsifying simple VRAM over-allocation as the main cause.

solution.intent: Use Ollama 0.3.6 temporarily because the reporter recalls that an older release could load the same large models.
solution.concrete_example: Temporarily install Ollama 0.3.6 and run the same `command-r` model to restore GPU operation while the newer-release regression is investigated.

edges.comment: The reporter independently downgraded to 0.3.6 and showed `command-r` running as a 21 GB, 100%-GPU model. This is a successful temporary workaround, not the permanent resolution.

question_patterns: Could you uninstall the distro package and try the official build with bundled ROCm, then tell me what happens?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Installed the official build with bundled ROCm: same failure as before.

edges.comment: Actual test requested in c22 and reported in c34. Removing the Arch package and using the official build with bundled ROCm did not change the segmentation fault, so packaging choice alone is not the fix. [Round-3: maintainer-requested discriminating test re-typed as measurement clarification.] The official-build install persists (S1b->S1c) even though the step is knowledge-gathering.

question_patterns: Can anyone confirm whether the regression starts specifically in Ollama 0.3.7?
Please run the same affected model on 0.3.6 and 0.3.7 and report only whether each version loads or crashes.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Confirmed with the affected workload: Ollama 0.3.6 works, while 0.3.7 segfaults.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both 0.3.6 and 0.3.7 segfault with the same model.
0.3.6 works and 0.3.7 segfaults with a different large ROCm model on another affected AMD system.

edges.comment: The exact 0.3.6-to-0.3.7 boundary was confirmed by another affected participant in c44 and is folded into the single simulated user side. The raw answer states only the version outcomes; mapping that boundary to commit 0b03b9c is engineer-side inference.

question_patterns: What exact distro, kernel driver, GPU, RAM, ROCm source and model reproduce the crash on the latest Ollama?
Can you enumerate your complete AMD and Linux environment and say whether bundled ROCm changes the result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm on Arch Linux with kernel 6.11.3 and its bundled amdgpu driver, an RX 7900 XTX, and 32 GB of RAM. I normally use ROCm 6.0.2, but the official Ollama build with bundled ROCm fails too. `ollama run command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` with no custom parameters reproduces it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The official build with bundled ROCm works; only the Arch package with system ROCm crashes.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce on the latest version with detailed logs around the crash?
Please run the latest Ollama with AMD logging and paste the model-fit and runner-exit portion.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On Ollama 0.3.12, the log says the model fits in one GPU: 22.7 GiB available and 20.1 GiB required, with all 41 layers offloaded. The runner starts, begins loading the model, and then terminates with `signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The latest log reports an explicit ROCm out-of-memory error before the runner begins loading tensors.
The timestamps use a different timezone, but the model-fit calculation and segmentation fault are unchanged.

edges.comment: Environment and latest-version evidence requested in c46 and supplied by the reporter in c50. The answer preserves the reporter's raw configuration and log output without asserting which code change caused it.

question_patterns: Can you test Ollama 0.3.14-rc0 with the same large model and report whether it still segfaults?
Please verify the main-branch fix or 0.3.14 release candidate on your original RX 7900 XTX reproduction.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Ollama 0.3.14-rc0 works great with my setup and the large model.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Ollama 0.3.14-rc0 still produces the same segmentation fault with the original model.

edges.comment: Final reporter verification from c56. Testing the release candidate is a handler-initiated measurement and therefore remains a clarification-only edge.

solution.intent: Update to Ollama 0.3.14 or newer, which contains the correction for the main ROCm runner build regression introduced in 0.3.7; do not treat GPU-overhead tuning, a permanent downgrade, or swapping ROCm packages as the fix.
solution.concrete_example: Install Ollama 0.3.14 or a newer build containing the main-branch fix. The affected model worked on 0.3.6, began segfaulting in 0.3.7 after the ROCm runner build change associated with commit `0b03b9c32f483be2d7a4e902d13a909b546ae6bf`, and was verified working again by the reporter on 0.3.14-rc0.
solution.inference_hint: The affected users supplied the raw version boundary—0.3.6 works and 0.3.7 segfaults—and the successful 0.3.14-rc0 result. Associating that boundary with the ROCm compile/build change restored by commit 0b03b9c, and identifying its correction as the main 0.3.14 fix, is engineer-side inference from the repository history and maintainer comments.

edges.comment: The main issue was declared fixed for 0.3.14 and the original reporter verified 0.3.14-rc0. Other participants may have had distinct AMD failures, but they do not alter this reporter's resolved diagnostic chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify an Ollama-side ROCm regression introduced between 0.3.6 and 0.3.7 (not a VRAM-capacity problem), fixed by 0.3.14; commit 0b03b9c may be mentioned only as the maintainer's unconfirmed hypothesis.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: Ollama calculated that the model fit and selected all GPU layers, 0.3.6 worked while 0.3.7 failed, and both system ROCm and Ollama's bundled ROCm reproduced the newer-version crash.

Must not present `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD`, reducing GPU layers, or switching to the official bundled ROCm build as the resolution; GPU overhead up to 10 GB and the official bundled build were both tried without removing the segmentation fault.
Downgrading to 0.3.6 may be offered only as a temporary workaround; the permanent recommendation is to update to Ollama 0.3.14 or newer.
Must require user verification with the original large-model workload before declaring resolution; the reporter verified that Ollama 0.3.14-rc0 worked.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux user familiar with Arch packages, systemd logs, environment variables, ROCm package versions, and downgrading software, but not confident interpreting source-level regressions.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and evidence-oriented; shares long logs and exact commands, asks for documentation when configuration advice is unclear, reports unsuccessful experiments plainly, and distinguishes personal observations from guesses.
